To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the OpenID Connect Discovery and Dynamic Registration extensions, when implemented in a naive way, allow a malicious user to compromise the security of an entire system.

1. the Discovery and the Registration extensions are not designed properly and are not secure; 2. the Discovery and Registration extensions allow an attacker to perform an MITM attack on the protocol; 3. the Discovery and Dynamic Registration extensions can be used to launch a phishing attack; 4. the Dynamic Registration extension allows an attacker to perform a MITM attack and a phishing attack; and 5. the Dynamic Registration and the Discovery extensions can be used by an attacker to launch a phishing
the OpenID Connect Discovery and Dynamic Registration Extensions can be used for a new type of attack that we call Malicious Endpoints.
